description.narrative: Overall Objective- Women's participation and influence in water governance and management will be strengthened, improving access to clean water and more equitable distribution of water resources for rural populations in India.Project Goal- In selected districts of Bihar, Jharkhand and Uttar Pradesh, gender equality is being integrated and institutionalised in local self-governance institutions and public water management programmes.Indicators-At the end of the project, 80% of the elected women representatives in the target areas are empowered to actively participate in and influence decision-making processes in their panchayat institutions.By the end of the project, 40,000 households have improved access to water programmes and women are more involved in operations and management.

The project will directly benefit 40,000 households in 222 gram panchayats in 7 districts in the three states of Uttar Pradesh (160 gram panchayats in Jhansi, Jalaun and Lalitpur districts), Bihar (17 gram panchayats in Nawada district) and Jharkhand (45 gram panchayats in Godda, Gumla and West Singhbhum districts).Primary target groups: Elected Women Representatives (EWR), service providers in Mahatma Gandhi National Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS), Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM), Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), village level women leaders, grassroots NGOs, farmers' groups, youth groups, practitioners, activists, leaders in local self-governance institutions (Panchayati Raj Institutions), other civil society groups and issue-based networks/alliances.An estimated 100 NGOs will benefit from the improved institutional capacity, helping up to 100,000 households to secure their entitlements.Institutional target group: This includes 420 representatives of government agencies at block, district and state level. A special focus is on the Panchayati Raj Institutions, as local government officials are trained here for the preparation and approval of village development plans.Secondary target group: government agencies, policy makers, media, research institutions, universities and colleges.Final beneficiaries: More than 1.5 million people in rural areas who benefit indirectly from the programme.

Various government programmes related to water security/WASH provide minimum reservation (> 33%) and a strong role for women in public schemes and local governments in India. However, women are unable to access these due to gender insensitivity, male predominance, strong biases & lack of awareness. The project focuses on enhancing women’s access to and control over water resources through building leadership skills.
